The '''2022 Kirklees Metropolitan Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022. One third of councillors—23 out of 69—on [[Kirklees Metropolitan Borough Council]] were elected. The election took place alongside [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections across the United Kingdom]].

Following the [[2021 Kirklees Metropolitan Borough Council election|previous council election in 2021]], no party held a majority of seats. Labour held 33, and ran a minority administration. The Conservatives held 19, the Liberal Democrats held 9, the Greens held 3 and independent councillors and councillors for local parties held the remaining five.

== Background ==
[[File:Kirklees UK local election 2018 map.svg|thumb|Result of the council election when these seats were last contested in 2018]]
[[File:Kirklees UK local election 2021 map.svg|thumb|Result of the most recent council election in 2021]]
The [[Local Government Act 1972]] created a two-tier system of metropolitan counties and districts covering [[Greater Manchester]], [[Merseyside]], [[South Yorkshire]], [[Tyne and Wear]], the [[West Midlands (county)|West Midlands]], and [[West Yorkshire]] starting in 1974. Kirklees was a district of the West Yorkshire metropolitan county.<ref name="guide">{{cite book |title=Local Government in England and Wales: A Guide to the New System |publisher=[[HMSO]] |year=1974 |isbn=0-11-750847-0 |location=London |page=7}}</ref> The [[Local Government Act 1985]] abolished the metropolitan counties, with metropolitan districts taking on most of their powers as [[Metropolitan borough|metropolitan boroughs]]. The [[West Yorkshire Combined Authority]] was established in 2014 and began electing the [[mayor of West Yorkshire]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=West Yorkshire devolution deal |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/west-yorkshire-devolution-deal |access-date=2022-01-22 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}}</ref>

Kirklees Council has generally been under [[no overall control]] or [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control since its creation, with the Conservatives controlling the council between 1976 and 1979. The council was under no overall control from 1999 until the [[2018 Kirklees Metropolitan Borough Council election|2018 election]], when Labour gained two seats to achieve an overall majority on the council. Labour's majority narrowed, with the party holding 35 seats following the [[2019 Kirklees Metropolitan Borough Council election|2019 election]]. Three Labour councillors resigned from their party in November 2020, citing national issues and linked by media to the suspension of the former Labour leader [[Jeremy Corbyn]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Labour loses majority on Kirklees Council as councillors quit the party |url=https://www.dewsburyreporter.co.uk/news/politics/labour-loses-majority-on-kirklees-council-as-councillors-quit-the-party-3041257 |access-date=2022-03-26 |website=www.dewsburyreporter.co.uk |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Earnshaw |first=Tony |date=2020-11-19 |title=Labour loses Kirklees Council majority after three councillors quit the party |url=https://www.examinerlive.co.uk/news/west-yorkshire-news/labour-loses-kirklees-council-majority-19309367 |access-date=2022-03-26 |website=YorkshireLive |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2021 Kirklees Metropolitan Borough Council election|most recent council election in 2021]], the council remained in no overall control with Labour winning 12 seats on 35.9% of the vote, the Conservatives winning 9 seats on 38.0% of the vote, the Liberal Democrats winning 2 seats on 10.2% of the vote, the Green Party winning one seat on 10.4% of the vote and the [[Heavy Woollen District Independents]] winning one seat with 0.4% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Earnshaw |first=Tony |date=2021-05-08 |title=Kirklees local election results: no party in overall control |url=https://www.examinerlive.co.uk/news/west-yorkshire-news/kirklees-local-election-results-no-20556841 |access-date=2022-03-26 |website=YorkshireLive |language=en}}</ref>

Positions up for election in 2022 were last [[2018 Kirklees Metropolitan Borough Council election|elected in 2018]]. In that election, 12 Labour councillors were elected, as were seven Conservatives, three Liberal Democrats, one Green and one independent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lavigueur |first=Nick |date=2018-05-04 |title=Kirklees Council election results 2018 - who won in your ward |url=https://www.examiner.co.uk/news/west-yorkshire-news/kirklees-council-election-results-2018-14614560 |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=YorkshireLive |language=en}}</ref>

== Campaign ==

The ''Local Democracy Reporting Service'' reported that Almondbury, Colne Valley, Dalton, Denby Dale, Dewsbury East, Golcar, Heckmondwike, Holme Valley North, and Lindley wards were "battlegrounds", and that the Liberal Democrats and Green Party were unlikely to support Labour if they needed to work with other parties having lost seats.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Earnshaw |first=Tony |date=2022-03-14 |title=How Kirklees could look after May's local elections |url=https://www.examinerlive.co.uk/news/how-kirklees-could-look-after-23366641 |access-date=2022-03-26 |website=YorkshireLive |language=en}}</ref> 

== Electoral process ==
The council elects its councillors in thirds, with a third being up for election every year for three years, with no election in the fourth year.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Local government structure and elections |language=en |work=GOV.UK |url=https://www.gov.uk/guidance/local-government-structure-and-elections#electoral-cycles |access-date=2018-04-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Election Timetable in England |url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/694598/Election_Timetable_in_England.pdf}}</ref> The election will take place by [[first-past-the-post voting]], with wards generally being represented by three councillors, with one elected in each election year to serve a four-year term.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in Kirklees aged 18 or over will be entitled to vote in the election. People who live at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, are entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities. Voting in-person at polling stations will take place from 07:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters will be able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.
